podcasts.name: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Return from Hiatus (2013)
podcast.body: Fall Out Boy returned from a hiatus in 2013 with the album "Save Rock and Roll," serving as a notable exception to the general decline of pop punk. "Fallout Boy, who actually returned from Mahayatus in 2013 with an album that they called Save Rock and Roll."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 2: The Role of Indie Rock

podcast.title: Fidget Spinners as Merch (2017)
podcast.body: In 2017, Fall Out Boy, like many other bands, offered branded fidget spinners as part of their merchandise. These items were identified as one of the hottest band merch trends of the year. "Everybody sold branded fidget spinners, arcade fire, David Bowie, Prince Black Flag, the misfits, Nirvana, Queens of the Stone Age, followed boy, weird."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 60 Mind-Blowing Facts About Music in 60 Minutes: 2017 Edition

podcast.title: Contemporary Powerpop (Possible)
podcast.body: Fall Out Boy is tentatively included as a potential contemporary Powerpop band, indicating that elements of the genre might be found in their sound. This highlights the genre's pervasive influence and its presence, even if subtle, in various modern acts. "Well we have Jimmy Eat World, OkGo, All American Rejects, Simple Plan, maybe Fallout Boy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Power Pop

podcast.title: Continued Touring
podcast.body: Fall Out Boy continued to be an active touring act into the 2010s, performing alongside other established pop punk bands. "So it was the offspring and Billy Towns and Fallout Boy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of Pop Punk: Part 2

podcast.title: Entire Band Clone Theory
podcast.body: Building on the Pete Wentz clone theory, some conspiracy theorists allege that all members of Fall Out Boy are dead and have been replaced by man-made humans. Additionally, it is claimed that the cloned Patrick Stump was originally born a woman. "Turns out that all of the members of follow up boy are dead Pete was just the last one to go and Oh, did I mention that bad-made Patrick Stump was actually born a woman?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Even More Rock Conspiracies

podcast.title: Influenced by Blink-182
podcast.body: Fall Out Boy is cited as an artist who owes something to Blink-182, indicating that Blink-182 served as an influential force in their musical development or career path. "Some 41 good Charlotte simple-plan panic at the disco, followed boy, headly, billy talent, you would meet six, paramour, you know, you get the idea."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

podcast.title: Joe Biden's Accidental Role in Band Formation
podcast.body: Fall Out Boy's existence is indirectly linked to Joe Biden. Pete Wentz's parents met while campaigning for Biden when he was running for Senator in the 1970s. A photograph even exists showing Biden posing with baby Pete Wentz. Therefore, without Biden's campaign, Wentz's parents might not have met, and Pete Wentz, and consequently Fall Out Boy, might not have formed. "Pete Wenz says his parents meant while campaigning for Biden when he was running for Senator in the 1970s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 60 Facts in 30 Minutes: 2020 Edition

podcast.title: Leading Emo Band
podcast.body: Fall Out Boy was identified as one of the bands that gained significant traction during the Emo boom of the 2000s. They were part of the trend where record labels actively signed Emo and Emo-influenced groups to capitalize on the genre's rising popularity. "Dashboard, confessional, taking back Sunday, panic at the disco, followed boy, story of the year, funeral for a friend, 30 seconds to Mars."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 15

podcast.title: Legacy of Mid-90s Punk Revival
podcast.body: Fall Out Boy is one of the bands whose existence can be directly attributed to the impact of the mid-1990s punk rock revival. "It's certainly not a stretch to say the groups like... Followed Boy... wouldn't have existed had it not been for what happened in the middle 1990s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 90s Part 6: The Punk Revival

podcast.title: Moved Away from Emo Sound
podcast.body: Fall Out Boy was cited as a band that moved away from their original emo sound by the early 2010s, along with Paramore and Panic! at the Disco, contributing to the genre's temporary decline. This shift was part of a larger trend as fans and bands evolved, though emo later saw a strong revival mid-decade. "Followed boy moved away from their original emo sound as did Paramore and Panic at the disco."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 4: The Revivals

podcast.title: Number One Records in 2010s
podcast.body: Fall Out Boy was among the artists, including Blink-182, Green Day, Coldplay, Jack White, Red Hot Chili Peppers, Slipknot, Queens of the Stone Age, Pearl Jam, Foo Fighters, U2, Linkin Park, Evanescence, and David Bowie, who achieved number one records during the 2010s. This demonstrated the continued success of rock acts in an era where hip hop was a dominant cultural force. "Link wanted a two Green Day Coldplay Jack White, Red Hotch-Lie Pepper, Slipp-Nont, Queens of the Stone Age, Pearl Jam, Foo Fighters, U2, Link and Park Follow Boy, Evan Essence, Queens of the Stone Age, and Bowie all had number one records over the course of the decade."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 4: The Revivals

podcast.title: Reunion for Touring
podcast.body: Fall Out Boy was one of many bands from past decades that reunited in the 21st century, a trend largely motivated by financial incentives. With declining CD sales impacting artist revenues, returning to the touring circuit offered a lucrative way to appeal to nostalgic fan bases and fill large venues. "The list of reunions is long."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 1: (100-91)

podcast.title: Shift Towards Pop
podcast.body: In the late 2000s, as pure pop gained dominance, Fall Out Boy consciously decided to "err on the side of pop when it came to writing new tunes." This strategic shift aimed to adapt to changing mainstream music trends. "This was the direction taken by Fallout Boy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of Pop Punk: Part 2

podcast.title: Shift from Emo Sound
podcast.body: After the peak of third wave emo, Fall Out Boy was noted as one of the bands that moved on to explore other sounds and styles, diverging from their original emo sound. "Others moved on to other sounds and styles, think panic at the disco and fallout boy in Paramore."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 3: Emo

podcast.title: Third Wave Emo Chart Success
podcast.body: Fall Out Boy was among the bands whose emo records achieved mainstream success during the third wave of emo (early 2000s), with their albums reaching the top 10 on charts. "Emo records from bands like...Fallout Boy... all rocketed into the top 10 on the album charts."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 3: Emo

xref.title: Influence on Pop Punk
xref.body: Blink-182 is considered one of the most influential pop punk bands of the 21st century. Their style and career trajectory have left a significant mark on numerous artists across the genre, inspiring bands like Sum 41, Good Charlotte, Simple Plan, Panic! At The Disco, Fall Out Boy, Hedley, Billy Talent, You Me At Six, and Paramore. "Blink has to be considered one of the most influential pop punk bands of the 21st century."
